title: Efficient Memory Side-Channel Protection for Embedding Generation in Machine Learning
problem: Embedding table lookups in ML models (DLRMs, LLMs) leak sensitive input features (user IDs, token indices) through memory access patterns, making them vulnerable to side-channel attacks; protecting these accesses with conventional ORAM incurs prohibitive overhead due to the massive size of embedding tables.
motivation: Privacy-preserving ML inference requires hiding memory access patterns to embedding tables, but embedding tables can be hundreds of gigabytes, making ORAM's O(log N) overhead per access impractical.
method: The paper evaluates three defenses against side-channel attacks (information leaking through memory access patterns): linear scan (reading every row of the embedding table—a lookup table for neural network parameters—to hide which row is actually used), ORAM (a technique that encrypts and reshuffles memory accesses to obscure patterns, but is expensive for huge tables), and Deep Hash Embedding (DHE), which computes the embedding through a neural network fed the index directly, eliminating the memory access signature. A hybrid scheme combines DHE for large tables (where computation cost is spread across many lookups) and linear scan for small tables, chosen per table based on measured performance tradeoffs.
key_novelty: The core innovation is replacing embedding table lookups with Deep Hash Embedding (DHE)—a neural network that computes embeddings from indices instead of fetching them from memory—which defends against side-channel attacks by eliminating the telltale memory access pattern rather than merely hiding it, yielding 4x speedup over optimized ORAM and 1116x memory footprint reduction.
contributions: Systematic comparison of three side-channel protection strategies for embedding tables: linear scan, ORAM, and DHE
Demonstration that DHE eliminates memory access patterns and simultaneously reduces model memory footprint by up to 1116x
Hybrid DHE+linear-scan scheme achieving 4x speedup over optimized ORAM for DLRM on Criteo datasets and up to 3.08x end-to-end speedup
Extension to LLMs showing DHE speeds up GPT-2 prompt prefill by up to 1.32x and decoding by up to 1.07x over ORAM

metrics.speedup: 4x for large DLRM embedding tables vs ORAM; up to 3.08x end-to-end vs optimized ORAM; 1.32x prefill and 1.07x decoding for GPT-2 vs ORAM

limitations: DHE introduces additional compute overhead for embedding generation that may not be acceptable for latency-critical inference at very high batch sizes.
primary_theme: compute-based DHE as memory side-channel protection for embedding table lookups
